text:
alex: Quick summary — I ran a region-by-region cost delta for Dedicated GPU capacity (H100/A100 mix) vs spot-backed autoscaling for hosted clusters. Wanted to surface the tradeoffs before the capacity commit conversation tomorrow.

maria: nice, do you have the high-level numbers?

alex: TL;DR: committed reserved capacity is ~25-35% cheaper than on-demand in us-west1 and europe-west4 when amortized over 12 months at our expected utilization (60-80%). In ap-southeast1 the discount narrows to ~10-15% because reserved pricing there is higher and spot reclaim rates are worse.

tariq: what about spot? can it beat reserved if we overprovision autoscaler headroom?
alex: spot lowers unit GPU cost by another ~20-30% in us-west1 and europe-west4, but reclaim churn increases effective application-level latency and increases cache misses for KV cache. For inference SLOs that need sub-50ms tail, we can't rely purely on spot for production-critical routes.

emma: any network egress/cross-region cost differences? that often bites Dedicated placement.
alex: yes — europe-west4 -> us-west1 egress per TB is ~3x higher than intra-region. If we colocate model serving with user traffic (region pinned) we avoid that. For multi-region fallback, the egress can offset spot savings quickly.

maria: did you include NVMe-local storage or model snapshot sync costs in the calc? those are nontrivial for H100 models.
alex: included a rough model: snapshot sync (weekly) + warm cache population + 10% snapshot delta. For H100 with 700GB model shards, snapshot transfer costs add ~8-12% to monthly bill in ap regions.

costbot: Billing anomaly detected: Estimated reserved-commitment break-even for europe-west4 at 12 months is 31% lower than on-demand at 70% utilization. See /billing/reports/2026-q1/region-breakdown (internal).

tariq: interesting — so ops decision leans reserved in US + EU core regions, spot for bursts in secondary regions?
emma: that matches my intuition. Also, we should prefer smaller commit terms (6 vs 12 mo) in ap-east to keep flexibility until demand stabilizes.
maria: any constraints on GPU SKUs by region? we've seen intermittent H100 capacity limits in europe-west4 the past 2 weeks.
alex: good call. europe-west4 has sporadic H100 shortages. For canary/Dedicated we should plan A100 fallbacks and a policy that pins customers to A100 variants if H100 unavailable. I'll add a routing rule: prefer H100, fallback to A100 with grace degradation and notif.
tariq: can we show a quick cost snippet for a 3-node H100 pool vs 3-node A100 pool in us-west1?
alex: sure, rough numbers:
```
us-west1 3xH100 (reserved 1yr): $4.2k/mo
us-west1 3xA100 (reserved 1yr): $2.8k/mo
spot 3xH100 avg: $1.9k/mo (but 18% reclaim)
```

emma: reclaim also increases request retries and KV cache warmup which reduces effective throughput — factoring that raises spot effective cost by ~10-20% for inference workloads.

maria: latency/regulatory: some EU customers require data residency. Those lines we must be 100% region pinned (no cross-region). So reserved there makes sense despite price.

alex: Agreed. Proposal:
- Commit reserved capacity (1yr) in us-west1 + europe-west4 based on 70% baseline utilization.
- Use spot pools for burst capacity and in secondary regions (ap-southeast1, sa-east1) with conservative reclaim margins.
- For regions with H100 scarcity (europe-west4), maintain an A100 fallback plan and a small buffer of reserved A100.
- Shorter commits (6mo) and more conservative quantities in APAC until we see stability.

tariq: +1. Also recommend we set up a daily cost delta alert comparing committed vs actual spend to catch over/under provisioning early.
costbot: Action created: /ops/tasks/7235 - "Region commit monitoring" assigned to eng-infra. Due 2026-04-05.
maria: one more: what's the impact on Redwood Dedicated SLAs? reserved helps with predictability, spot does not. Enterprise customers with SLAs should be pinned to reserved pools only.
alex: yes — Dedicated SLA customers will be placed on reserved pools, non-SLA/public hosted routes can use spot for cost savings. We'll add a placement policy in the routing matrix.
emma: can we surface these numbers in Console (per-region breakdown + commit recommendation)? Product can use that for renewals.
alex: I'll ship a short spreadsheet + export to /shared/eng-infra/region-commit-plan-1765504321.csv and sync with Product.
tariq: ok next steps?
alex: 1) I'll drop the spreadsheet and add the fallback policy PR for routing. 2) Maria/tariq: decide exact commit quantities for us-west1/europe-west4 (I'll provide a suggested start). 3) Ops: enable the daily cost delta alerts (Costbot created task). 4) Product: we expose the regional recommendation in Console.
maria: I'll take the us-west1 numbers and ping finance for budget signoff.
tariq: I'll run a quick simulation on reclaim churn effect on tail latency tonight.
emma: thanks — this is helpful. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks everyone. I'll post the CSV in ~10m and @maria I'll DM the recommended numbers.
